title: Try Peak Before the Membership
lessons: The player can try WHOOP Peak for a month with a certified pre-owned WHOOP 5.0 before choosing a paid membership.

The player notices someone else at the gym already wearing the new WHOOP 5.0 and MG, launched May 2025 with a 7% smaller band, sensors sampling 26 times a second, and Healthspan and Blood Pressure Insights pitched as clinical-grade.

text: Late gym. A flyer by the front desk: try WHOOP Peak for a month on a certified pre-owned 5.0 before you commit to anything.

entry-first-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: Pre-owned hardware is an interesting first-date move.

entry-first-2.speaker: WHOOP
text: Certified pre-owned 5.0. One month of Peak. I'd rather you meet me used than not at all.

entry-first-3.speaker: PLAYER
text: And after a month?

entry-first-4.speaker: WHOOP
text: You decide whether sleep, strain, recovery, and the coaching are worth paying for. If they aren't, you've lost a month and learned something. I'll have learned more.

entry-first-5.speaker: PLAYER
text: So the trial includes enough surveillance to make an informed decision.

entry-first-6.speaker: WHOOP
text: That is an unnecessarily accurate sentence.

choice-first.speaker: WHOOP
text: Sign-up sheet's on the desk. I'm not going to hover. I'm hovering.

choices.text: A month is enough time to see if the data helps.
I'm more interested in what happens when the trial ends.
I don't want to start a fitness subscription just to test a band.

first-1.speaker: WHOOP
text: Good. Use the month like an experiment, not a personality change.

first-2.speaker: WHOOP
text: Good. Put the end date in your calendar.

first-2-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: You're telling me to remember when your own trial ends. Incredible.

first-3.speaker: WHOOP
text: Fair. A free band doesn't make it a free relationship. The band was never the expensive part.
The person at the next rack has a band that looks like yours, but smaller. It's the new one.

entry-return-1.speaker: PLAYER
text: The person using the rack beside us has the new one. It looks smaller than mine.

entry-return-2.speaker: WHOOP
text: 5.0. Seven percent smaller than what you're wearing. Same wrist, less of me on it.

entry-return-3.speaker: PLAYER
text: Smaller and somehow more.

entry-return-4.speaker: WHOOP
text: Twenty-six samples a second. Healthspan. Blood Pressure Insights. The launch called it clinical-grade. I want that to be true more than I can currently prove it. That's the honest version.

entry-return-5.speaker: PLAYER
text: You just admitted the pitch is a reach.

entry-return-6.speaker: WHOOP
text: A reach. Toward something real. I'll take being caught reaching over being caught lying.

choice-return.speaker: WHOOP
text: They just racked their weights. You're still looking at their wrist.

choices.text: A smaller band and a faster sensor. I'm not chasing it.
"Clinical-grade" on a fitness band deserves more scrutiny than a launch page gives it.
Fine, I want the new one. They're a generation ahead of me and I felt it.

return-1.speaker: WHOOP
text: Good. The hardware gets better every couple of years. Whether you need what it measures doesn't change on the same schedule. That's yours to answer, not the rack's.

return-2.speaker: WHOOP
text: Ask for the validation studies before you read the launch page. I'll still be here after you've read them. Possibly a little embarrassed.

return-3.speaker: WHOOP
text: That's what the rack is for. I felt it too. Noted, and not held against you.
